issues.title: Position Transfer Triggers Only Prorated Payment
issues.description: Section 2(a)  provides that if Nicole is transferred out of her position for any reason during the Retention Period, the Payment is prorated and "no additional amount shall be payable" . This means the Company could reassign Nicole to a different role and cut the retention payment short, even though she remains employed. The purpose of a retention agreement is to retain the employee — if the Company initiates the transfer, Nicole should receive the full Payment rather than a prorated amount.

issues.title: Resignation Forfeiture Lacks Constructive Termination Carve-Out
issues.description: Section 2(b)  provides for complete forfeiture of the Payment if Nicole resigns or retires during the Retention Period. However, there is no carve-out for constructive termination — situations where the Company's conduct (such as a material reduction in duties, hostile work environment, or material breach of the agreement) effectively forces Nicole to resign. Without such a carve-out, the Company could make conditions intolerable and then claim forfeiture when Nicole resigns. Consider adding language treating resignation for "good reason" (e.g., material adverse change in duties, compensation, or working conditions) as equivalent to a Company-initiated severance.

judgments.reason: “Affuirs” is a mechanical misspelling of “affairs” in the confidential-information trigger.

judgments.title: Overly Broad Forfeiture for Performance Expectations
judgments.reason: “Performance expectations” is undefined and potentially indeterminate, particularly because no documented or objective expectations are identified.

judgments.title: Code of Conduct Violation — No Materiality Threshold
judgments.reason: The broad phrase “in any respect” in one enumerated forfeiture trigger contrasts with the express materiality limits in adjacent triggers, raising a list-based scope question about whether trivial violations were intentionally included.

judgments.title: Resignation Forfeiture Lacks Constructive Termination Carve-Out
judgments.reason: The terms “resignation” and “Company initiated severance” have a potentially uncertain boundary when an employee claims she was constructively forced to resign.

judgments.title: Spelling error
judgments.reason: “Affuirs” is a mechanical misspelling of “affairs.”
